provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: In the original orientation, the generator draws a cyan (8) pixel set on a black (0) background. The output erases it and redraws the same shape one row lower in red (2). The factory works out the visible shift direction from d4. A row reversal negates the column component of the direction. Each clockwise rotation maps a direction (dr,dc) to (dc,-dr). So 'down' becomes left, up or right depending on the rotation. The colour roles become constants: palette[0] is the background and palette[2] is the recolour target. Every non-background cell counts as part of the object, which covers palette[8] cells. The emitted program builds a background canvas of the same rectangular shape. It then stamps the recolour constant at each object cell moved by (DR, DC), in visible coordinates. Demonstrations are not needed and are ignored.
draft_notes.limitations: Cells that would leave the grid are dropped. This matches the archived solver's bottom-edge behaviour, but the constructor never produces that case: it places the object so at least one row of space remains in the shift direction. The background is taken as the fixed palette[0] constant rather than the most frequent colour; the two agree for every generator output. Any non-background colour in the input is treated as part of the object. The approved fixtures agree with the uniform rule, with no contradictions, and the generator has no hidden tie-breaks or indexing defects. This factory has not been tested.

independent_source_review.mechanism: Every non-background cell (input ink palette[8]) is erased and redrawn shifted one step in a fixed direction in colour palette[2]. Natively the direction is down (dr=+1, dc=0). The factory turns d4 into a visible direction constant (DR, DC). The emitted solver then stamps NEW at (y+DR, x+DC) for each non-BG cell, directly in visible coordinates.
evidence: Constructor: rows come from random_pixels(width, height), which yields r in range(height). The object is offset by row = randint(0, size-height-1), so the deepest row is at most size-2 and output[r+1][c] is always in bounds. No input cell ever sits on the bottom row.
randint bounds are valid for every size in 3..7. The maximum height is (size+1)//2, which is at most size-1, so size-height-1 >= 0 and col's upper bound size-width >= 0.

Labels depend only on the visible input cells: each cyan cell maps to the red cell directly below it. The pixel sampling is random, but the label is a deterministic function of the input, with no hidden latent, tie-break or ordering dependence. Disconnected or scattered pixel sets are handled cellwise, the same in the constructor and the solver.

Every grid is a single colour on a uniform background: grids() fills with 0 and only cyan is drawn. The fixed BG=palette[0] therefore matches the archived most-common background heuristic. Even a fully filled object region (at most 4x4 in 7x7) cannot outnumber the background.

Factory direction algebra: a clockwise rotation (r,c)->(c,H-1-r) maps a displacement (dr,dc) to (dc,-dr), so down becomes left. Row reversal negates dc, which is a no-op on (1,0) itself. Flip-then-rotate versus rotate-then-flip would differ for odd rotations with a flip. The host audit's 8000 augmented checks (1000 pairs x 8) and 16 fixture variants passed, which indicates the factory's composition order matches the host D4 convention.
The emitted solver has no untransform/native-solve/retransform wrapper. It uses only specialised colour and direction constants on the visible grid.

The recolour target (2) is a fixed rule colour, consistent in every demonstration, so it is not an arbitrary per-episode lookup. The episode colour-evidence checks do not target this task, and none are needed.
nonblocking_limits: The out-of-bounds drop in the solver is a defensive branch the constructor never reaches: the object always leaves at least one free row or column in the shift direction. The demonstrations therefore never test edge behaviour.
Any non-background colour is treated as object ink. Only palette[8] occurs in the generator's domain.
BG is the fixed palette[0] rather than the most frequent colour. These are equivalent on every constructor output.
The direction composition order for reflected variants (d4>=4) was verified only through the host audit's passing augmented checks, not from host transform source supplied here.
required_context_checks: Confirm that the host D4 convention applies the row reversal before the d4%4 clockwise rotations, consistent with the passing 8000 augmented checks, so that DR/DC are correct for d4 in {5,7}.

draft_notes.host_review: Reviewed mechanism and limitations. Confirmed augmentation.py uses a bijective palette, horizontal flip followed by clockwise turns; audit.py checks every D4, not only its final reported d4=7. Episode-wide D4 ambiguity gate is active. Out-of-domain fallbacks do not justify unverified inputs; every export still executes the program on every pair.
